_comment: How Node and Python read /services/agentHarness/approvals (approvals-document.schema.json). `rules`: one layer, valid or not, normalized to {classes, tools} (writes sets write and execute, the stricter wins). `documents`: the effective policy for a run of (orgId, agentKey) over the deployment's layers (default, then agents[agentKey]) - per class the strictest over every layer, per tool the strictest tool rule (a call's decision is the stricter of the two) - and the document's status. A layer that cannot be read is writes-ask; a document whose top level the schema refuses is writes-ask as a whole. SEC2: a layer's `flow` normalizes to {level, above} (above defaults to public) and appears only when set; the effective `flow` lists the strictest rules over every layer's (off is none; a rule another covers - as strict, from as low a threshold - is dropped; ordered by threshold, then level), present only when a layer has one. The deployment's own rule (HARNESS_FLOW_GUARD) is not in the document and joins in the worker.
